issues.description: In the template for Exercise 1 the Grover assembly method is named build_grover(...) but the class run() implementation calls self.grover_circuit(...). This name mismatch means a student implementing the intended assembly method as named in the template (build_grover) will still have run() attempt to call a non-existent method (grover_circuit), causing runtime/usage failures and confusion about the required method name. The solution implementation uses grover_circuit(...), so the template's build_grover name is inconsistent with both run() and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make method naming consistent: either rename the template method build_grover(...) to grover_circuit(...) or update run() to call build_grover(...). Align the template method name with the solution (grover_circuit) and with the problem statement task names so students implement and invoke the same method.

issues.description: In the two-qubit Grover exercise template the method that builds the Grover circuit is named build_grover (template), but the run() helper calls self.grover_circuit(...) and the reference solution implements grover_circuit. This mismatch between build_grover and grover_circuit creates an unintended naming inconsistency: students will be unsure which method to implement and the provided run() will fail if they implement build_grover as defined in the template. The problem statement task refers to building the Grover circuit (Exercise 1.5) and the solution uses grover_circuit, so the template's build_grover name appears to be an accidental divergence.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier: either rename the template method build_grover to grover_circuit or change the run() call to use build_grover. Prefer renaming build_grover -> grover_circuit in the template to match the solution and the exercise task naming, so students see a consistent method name across problem, template, and solution.
